instance.finding_key: packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts::the lone-dash setext exemption is unconditional (not scoped to list context), so every existing note using the valid single-dash setext h2 form `title\n-` silently stops rendering as a heading.

finding.summary: The lone-dash setext exemption is unconditional (not scoped to list context), so every existing note using the valid single-dash setext H2 form `Title\n-` silently stops rendering as a heading.
finding.evidence:
`const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1;` at list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:104 has no guard on `state.blkIndent`, `state.parentType`, or whether a list is open. It fires identically for a top-level `Title\n-`, which is a perfectly ordinary CommonMark setext H2. Note content is stored as raw markdown in Yorkie (docs/design/notes/notes.md:96 — "one flat string in one `Text` CRDT"), so this re-renders *all already-stored* notes, not just newly typed ones: the heading becomes a paragraph followed by a stray empty `
`. The consumer left describing the old contract is docs/design/notes/notes.md:296-297, which asserts "Multi-dash `---` and `=` setext underlines are untouched, so ordinary setext headings still render" — single-dash setext headings are ordinary setext headings and no longer render. The change's own plan file (docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-todo.md:62) lists "top-level lone dash" as a case to cover, and no test in the added block (preview.test.ts:151-196) exercises it. Consider gating `isLoneDash` on being inside a list / non-zero `blkIndent`.
